The example claims are thin, and an investigator would still have to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Headline says 99215 is billed above expectation 'in every complexity tier', but the card shows 99215 shares only about 1.3 to 3.5 times the all-provider share by tier (e.g. 0.073 vs 0.053 at 2 conditions is about 1.4x), so 'two to three times in every tier' is overstated.","Rationale says 'two to three times the all-provider share in every complexity tier'; ratios are 3.2x, 2.4x, 1.4x, 1.7x, 1.7x, 2.1x, so the claim is inaccurate for tiers 2-5.","'Provider-wide billing habit' is a strong inference given the plain z-score is only 1.37, and it conflicts with the inconclusive leaning.","Headline says the returned charts support the billed level, but only 5 documented 99215s exist; 'support' is based on tiny n, and one has minutes 'not recorded'. The rationale does acknowledge thinness, but the headline still frames it as supportive.","Claim C0082768 is cited as a supported low-complexity example, which is fine, but the three M0034839 claim IDs are not all in the cited_claim_ids, and the formal cited examples (C0082387, C0082395) are not documented claims and do not illustrate the narrative about high-MDM documentation.","The 11% comparison rate (all_provider_rate for 99215) is used, but 'comparison providers' is not defined on the card; a minor ambiguity.","Next steps are generic ('request larger sample', 're-screen') and do not name the specific claims to request that the rationale lists (M0034839 visits, 0-condition visits); the actionable step is buried in the rationale.","The summary does not flag that the 0 documented below-billed result and the 1 of 20 note-data discrepancy are statistically uninformative at this sample size beyond a brief remark."]}
